sheet-45-1.description: The lower half of the sheet shows the north-western part of Holly Beach (today Wildwood) in a strip five blocks deep, from West Baker Avenue at the top to West Andrews Avenue at the bottom, and from Mediterranean Avenue on the left edge across Susquehanna and Hudson Avenues and Railroad Avenue to Arctic Avenue on the right edge. Otten's Harbor, a straight canal, takes the place of an avenue between West Montgomery and West Burk Avenues, running from Mediterranean Avenue to a dead end just short of Railroad Avenue. The drawing is a lot plan rather than a built-up district: almost every block is divided into numbered 25 ft lots with block numbers (89, 90, 91, 80, 81, 82, 71, 72, 73, 61, 62, 63 and others), street widths of 50 and 60 ft are lettered, and only a scattering of buildings stands on them, mostly one and two storey frame dwellings, a few with stables or sheds, the densest group in block 91 on Hudson Avenue and in the narrow blocks between Railroad and Arctic Avenues, where Davis Avenue crosses the strip. The scale bar (100 ft to an inch) is printed inside Otten's Harbor at the left, the compass rose in block 100 at the top right, and the numbers 37 and 39 at the right edge refer to the adjoining sheets. The heavy line along the top separates this part from the inset and the Middle Township turnpike drawn above it.
notes: Railroad Av. is modern Park Boulevard (OpenStreetMap), built on the old railroad line.
Mediterranean Av. is split in OpenStreetMap: 'Mediterranean' north of Otten's Harbor (at West Montgomery and West Baker), 'Mediterranean Avenue' to the south.
Davis Av. (between Railroad and Arctic Avenues) has no modern street of that name in the reference data.
Park Boulevard / West Baker Avenue was excluded: the compass rose is drawn in that junction.

Single sheet (N.J.C.M. vol. 4, sheet 45), 100 ft to an inch. Despite the title, mostly Holly Beach (Wildwood): part 1 the lower half, West Baker to West Andrews Avenues from Mediterranean to Arctic Avenue (Railroad Av. = Park Boulevard), with Otten's Harbor; part 2 an inset framed in the upper right, Niagara to Mediterranean Avenues, same angle, unbuilt lots; part 3 the Middle Township part in the upper left, the turnpike (modern West Rio Grande Avenue) on a wooden bridge over Grassy Sound with buildings on piles, drawn along the road at its own angle and placed by hand. Detector ink_below_paper 100 (138 found 6 points on part 1, none on part 2).

sheet-45-2.description: An inset in the upper right of the sheet, framed by a heavy line, continues Holly Beach (today Wildwood) one block westward from the lower half: the blocks between Niagara Avenue and Mediterranean Avenue from West Baker Avenue down to West Andrews Avenue, together with a strip of block 87 1/2 west of Niagara Avenue along West Baker Avenue and the eastern end of blocks 69, 59 1/2 and 50 1/2 west of Niagara below the turnpike. It is drawn at the same scale and angle as the lower half, so Mediterranean Avenue at its right edge is the same street as at the left edge of the lower half. Otten's Harbor crosses the inset from Niagara Avenue to Mediterranean Avenue between West Montgomery and West Burk Avenues; the number 45 printed in it is the sheet number. All blocks are laid out in numbered 25 ft lots (blocks 96 1/2, 97, 87 1/2, 88, 79, 70, 69, 60, 59 1/2, 50 1/2, 51) and no buildings are drawn: this was still unbuilt land on the edge of the marsh. In the lower left the shore of Grassy Sound winds through blocks 69, 59 1/2 and 50 1/2, cutting off their western lots, and a small creek enters block 51 from West Andrews Avenue. The name Holly Beach is lettered at the top right. A note at the left edge of Otten's Harbor marks the end of the turnpike bridge from the mainland, which is drawn as a separate part to the left.
notes: No buildings are drawn in this part; all control is from the street grid (four Mediterranean Avenue junctions detected, Niagara Avenue / West Baker Avenue hand-picked).
Niagara Avenue / West Montgomery Avenue was excluded: the inset frame runs down the west side of Niagara Avenue there and the detector placed the junction about 16 ft east of the drawn centre.
West Burk and West Andrews Avenues no longer reach Niagara Avenue in OpenStreetMap.

sheet-45-3.description: The upper left of the sheet, under the heading Middle Township, Cape May County, shows the turnpike from the mainland (lettered Turnpike to Main Land) where it crosses Grassy Sound to Holly Beach on a wooden bridge built on piles. The road runs straight across the part as a broad yellow band and has a draw span over the deep water channel near its east end; a note at that end says the Rio Grand Inn is about 500 feet further on, on sheet 34. Along both sides of the bridge stand small buildings on piles reached by short walks: one, one-and-a-half and two storey frame dwellings, boat houses, a fish and boat house at the east end and, north of the road near the channel, a long double row of boat houses on a pier. Everything is surrounded by the open water of Grassy Sound, tinted blue around the buildings, and a note says all buildings are built on piles; the land beyond the left edge is noted as vacant. A dashed line marks the course of the deep water channel crossing the bridge diagonally. The north arrow in the lower left points to magnetic north, about seven degrees anticlockwise of true north. The heavy lines on the right and below separate this part from the Holly Beach inset and the lower half of the sheet, which are drawn at a different angle.
notes: The turnpike is modern West Rio Grande Avenue (CR 624); New Jersey Route 47 (Wildwood Boulevard) now crosses the sound on a new alignment just north of it.

Placed by a two-point helmert from the road line and the printed distance of about 500 ft to the Rio Grand Inn (Holly Beach 1909 sheet 34); the position along the road may be off by up to about 50 m. Modern lots along West Rio Grande Avenue match the drawn rows of buildings.
The part is drawn about 17 degrees from the Holly Beach street grid, along the road itself.
